title: SpaceX cleared to fly Starship again after booster failure in May
slides: SpaceX got FAA approval for Starship—but what changed?
The May failure destroyed the Super Heavy booster mid-flight.
The fix was simpler than anyone expected: a single fuel filter.
Your next launch might not need months of re-design anymore.
Rocket flaws can hide in parts you never think to check.
thread_text:
The Filter That Saved Starship

SpaceX got FAA approval for the next Starship launch after fixing a single fuel filter.

A Booster Lost to Dust

The May failure destroyed the Super Heavy booster because a clogged filter starved the engine.

Months of Work, One Part

Engineers found the culprit in a fuel line component nobody thought to inspect.

The Fix That Changes Launches

Your next launch won't need months of re-design if you check the simplest parts first.

What Are You Not Checking?

Rocket flaws hide in parts you never think to inspect. How many are in your own code or pipeline?

instagram.caption:
SpaceX traced a mid-flight booster explosion to one tiny fuel filter—and now the FAA has let them fly again. ⚙️

A clogged filter starved the Super Heavy engines, costing months of work. Engineers found the culprit in a part nobody thought to inspect. 🚀

If you're shipping software or running pipelines, your biggest failure might be hiding in a component you've never audited. 🔍

What cheap, overlooked dependency in your own stack could bring down your next launch?
